title: Expanding Logical Space Freely: A Memory-efficient Mapping Table Design for Compressional SSDs
problem: Reducing memory footprint of Logical-to-Physical (L2P) address mapping tables in compressional SSDs, which compress logical pages to improve capacity but increase mapping table size and pressure on in-SSD memory.
motivation: Compressional SSDs expand usable logical space but complicate Flash Translation Layer (FTL) design by inflating L2P mapping tables; bloated mapping tables degrade I/O performance and consume limited in-SSD memory.
method: N-to-1 L2P mapping table design consolidates multiple logical entries into single entries, eliminating duplication of physical page numbers when a physical page contains multiple compressed logical pages. Promotion/demotion mechanisms enable entries to migrate across pages with different compression ratios; compression-aware garbage collection algorithm minimizes copy operations for partially invalid physical pages due to N-to-1 mapping.
key_novelty: Novel N-to-1 mapping table design that consolidates compressed logical pages into single table entries, with dynamic promotion/demotion for varying compression ratios.
contributions: N-to-1 L2P mapping table design eliminating duplication in compressional SSDs
Promotion/demotion mechanisms for dynamic compression ratio adaptation
Compression-aware garbage collection minimizing partial invalidation overhead
Improved mapping table cache hit ratio and reduced I/O latency

metrics.other: Significantly reduced mapping table size; improved cache hit ratio and reduced I/O latency (specific numbers not provided)

limitations: Abstract does not provide numerical performance comparisons.
primary_theme: Memory-efficient L2P mapping for compressional SSDs via N-to-1 consolidation
